extractions.quote: The following muscles were bilaterally examined: deltoideus, biceps brachii, flexor carpi radialis, thenar muscles, lumbar paraspinal muscles, gluteus maximus, hamstrings, quadriceps, tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius-soleus complex.

extractions.value: Nerve conduction studies (NCS) were performed with supramaximal percutaneous nerve stimulation and surface electrode recording. EMG was performed using a pair of 10-mm diameter Ag/Ag Cl electrodes placed 2-4 cm apart longitudinally over the muscle bellies and standard Medelec concentric needle electrodes. Muscles were examined at rest and during a slight sustained voluntary contraction of about 20% of maximal isometric force (MIF). Cortical stimulation was performed at 40% above each muscle resting motor threshold. Long latency reflexes (LLRs) were elicited in leg muscles.
extractions.quote: Nerve conduction studies (NCS) were performed with supramaximal percutaneous nerve stimulation

In our patient 0. 8-1 mV amplitude and 50-55 ms latency LLRs were evoked in proximal muscles "at rest". LLRs of comparable amplitude and latency could be evoked in normal subjects only when the target muscles were contracting at about 50% of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC).

extractions.value: TMS revealed a distinctive motor evoked potential (MEP) pattern in proximal lower limb muscles consisting of markedly increased MEP amplitudes and MEP/M ratios, reduced excitability thresholds, and absent silent period. Treatment with benzodiazepine and baclofen normalized both the clinical picture and the MEP values.
extractions.quote: TMS may be useful both as a diagnostic tool and to monitor the response to drug treatment.
